data.name: VersionsHint
data.value: Steam keeps only one version of the game installed. To keep an older version next to it (for profiles whose mods haven't been updated yet): in Steam, open the game's Properties → Game Versions & Betas and pick that version. When Steam has finished downloading, click Keep a copy, then switch Steam back to the latest version. Keep copies on the same drive as the game: there they share every file that stays the same, so only the files an update changes take space.

data.name: VersionsLaunchNote
data.value: Copies are started directly, not through Steam, so Steam's launch options don't apply to them, and Steam must be running. Each profile picks its version in the Profiles tab.

data.name: VersionsConfirmShare
data.value:
Keep {0} {1} in {3}?
On this drive the copy shares the game's files ({2}) with the Steam install, so it needs almost no space now. When Steam updates the game, the copy keeps the old versions of the files that change, and only those take space (Steam's update needs that much free space).
Don't start the game or let Steam update it until this is finished, and don't edit files in the copy: shared files are the Steam install's files too.

data.name: VersionsConfirmPack
data.value:
Pack {0}?
Dispatch keeps only the data this version doesn't share with the Steam install ({1}) and shares the rest with it. A copy one or two versions old usually shrinks to about a tenth.
Before each play, Dispatch rebuilds the full game folder: that takes a few minutes and about {2} of free space while you play. It's removed again when the game closes.
The copy's files in {3} are deleted only after the packed copy has been read back and matches them byte for byte.

Steam has updated since it was packed, so it holds on to {1} of old Steam files. Packing it again against the Steam install ({2}) frees whatever the new version still shares.
